The role defines and monitors SLOs, instruments platforms for observability, leads incident response through to permanent prevention, and applies AI and automation for anomaly detection, predictive alerting and self-healing. It also coaches platform engineering teams in reliability practice and error-budget discipline. The role sits in Reliability Engineering & Operations and is deployed into a platform domain while drawing on the central capability, so it holds the central reliability standard inside a team it does not report to. Platform build and engineering direction sit with the Principal Engineers and the Engineering Director, the major incident process sits with the Major Incident Manager, and the reliability standard itself is set by the Reliability Engineering Senior Director. Reliability targets are held jointly with the Platform Manager rather than imposed on them. ROLE SCALE AND COMPLEXITY This is a senior enterprise reliability leadership role operating across globally distributed, business-critical cloud and hosting services. The post holder is accountable for setting technical direction, resolving systemic and ambiguous reliability risks, and influencing prioritisation across multiple platform teams, suppliers and geographies without relying on direct line authority. The role manages a portfolio of interdependent services with material operational, regulatory, cyber, resilience and financial consequences. It shapes investment and supplier decisions and may influence or govern an annual technology and service portfolio of up to approximately GBP 23 million, where applicable to the assigned scope. MARKET SCOPE Global scope, supporting business operations across regions, countries and markets in which GSK operates. The role establishes consistent reliability outcomes across regional delivery teams while accommodating local regulatory, data-residency, business-continuity and market-criticality requirements. Key Responsibilities Define and monitor SLOs for the platforms served, and instrument those platforms for observability so reliability is measured rather than assumed. Apply AI and automation for anomaly detection, predictive alerting and self-healing, so that recurring conditions are handled without human intervention. Lead incident response for the platforms served, and drive root-cause resolution through to permanent prevention rather than closing on restoration. Improve resilience through capacity, failover and recovery engineering, and test recovery rather than documenting it. Reduce operational toil through automation and reusable tooling, working the identified manual task and toil candidates and evidencing the effort removed. Close observability coverage gaps for the platforms served, prioritising by the reliability risk each gap leaves unmeasured. Coach platform engineering teams in reliability practice and error-budget discipline, so reliability is built in rather than inspected in. Track reliability metrics against SLOs and team OKRs, and act on the trend rather than only reporting it. Support reliability oversight of supplier-run services, holding partner-operated components to the same SLOs as internal ones. Hold the central reliability standard while deployed in a platform domain, escalating to the Reliability Engineering Senior Director where local pressure would erode it. Feed reliability evidence into the platform backlog held by the Product Owner, so that resilience work competes on stated risk rather than on goodwill. Hold the boundaries with the Principal Engineers on platform build, the Major Incident Manager on the major incident process, and the Platform Manager on the reliability targets the platform commits to. Set the multi-year reliability strategy and engineering roadmap for the assigned cloud and hosting portfolio, translating enterprise risk and business priorities into funded reliability outcomes. Own cross-platform reliability governance, including service tiering, SLO policy, error-budget decisions, resilience exceptions and common engineering standards across internal and supplier-operated services. Lead resolution of complex, high-impact and systemic failure modes spanning cloud, hosting, network, security, applications and third-party dependencies, with authority to convene senior technical and service leaders. Provide evidence-based recommendations for investment, risk acceptance and supplier performance decisions, including prioritisation across a material service portfolio and, where delegated, spend of up to approximately GBP 25 million. AIOps and operations automation, covering anomaly detection, predictive alerting and self-healing. Why is this level of Education Required? An engineering grounding is needed because the role writes the automation and instrumentation itself and must be credible to platform engineers whose systems it is changing. Job-Related Experience Overall 15 Years and typically 10-12+ years in infrastructure, cloud, platform or reliability engineering, including significant experience leading enterprise-scale reliability outcomes across multiple teams or service domains. 5+ years of hands-on SRE, Reliability Engineering, or Cloud Operations experience. Experience supporting large-scale production cloud and hosting environments. Experience owning operational reliability for critical business services. Proven record of improving service availability, resiliency, and operational efficiency. Demonstrated accountability for globally distributed, 24x7, business-critical services and for decisions with material operational, regulatory, customer or financial impact. Proven ability to influence Directors, Senior Directors and VP-level stakeholders, including presenting options, quantified risk, trade-offs and investment recommendations. Experience governing strategic suppliers and complex service ecosystems, with exposure to substantial technology budgets or portfolios; direct budget ownership is desirable but not mandatory where strong investment influence is evidenced. Track record of setting technical direction, leading through ambiguity and developing senior engineering capability across organisational and geographic boundaries. Reliability & Operations Experience defining and operating: SLIs , SLOs, Error Budgets, Operational KPIs Experience leading: Major incident response, post-incident reviews, Root-cause analysis , Capacity management, Resiliency and recovery testing.
